name: CHRONIQ
description: Background: Mobile health (mHealth) applications are increasingly used to support chronic disease management, yet concerns remain regarding their quality, safety, and practical value. Existing evaluation tools, such as Mobile App Rating Scale (MARS), Enlight, and the Multidimensional App Quality Assessment Tool for Health-Related Apps (AQUA), offer useful insights but do not fully address the long-term, information-intensive, and service-oriented demands of chronic disease contexts. This study validated the Chronic Disease Mobile Health Application Quality Evaluation Framework (CHRONIQ) framework as a practical tool for assessing the quality of mHealth apps for chronic disease in South Africa. Methods: A quantitative survey design was used, and 201 usable responses were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Results: The results supported eight of nine hypothesised relationships. System quality and service quality (SEQ) were positively associated with engagement quality (EQ), while EQ was positively associated with user satisfaction. User satisfaction showed significant positive relationships with intention to use, health outcomes, and net benefits. Bootstrapped mediation analysis further showed that EQ partially mediated the relationships between system quality and user satisfaction and between SEQ and user satisfaction. In contrast, the indirect effect of information quality through EQ was not significant.
